references.text: Moses tells the people that the Lord will fight for them, a direct parallel to the promise in Deuteronomy 1:30
The Lord fought for Israel against the Egyptians at the Red Sea, which is the historical example Moses refers to
Moses repeats that the Lord your God fights for you, the same promise as in 1:30
The Lord goes with the people to fight their enemies and give them victory
The Lord fought for Israel, a fulfillment of the promise that God will fight for his people
The Lord, the God of Israel, fought for Israel during the conquest of Canaan
Joshua reminds the people that the Lord your God has fought for you
The Lord your God fights for you, as he had promised
The battle belongs to the Lord; he will give the enemies into Israel's hand
The Lord does not save by sword and spear, for the battle belongs to the Lord
The Lord went before the people in a pillar of cloud and fire, showing that he goes before them
The Lord sends his angel ahead of the people to lead them and fight for them
